newsitem.title: UK: Frigid temperatures keep heat under oil price.
newsitem.headline: Frigid temperatures keep heat under oil price.

text.p: Forecasts for continued frigid temperatures on both sides of the Atlantic pushed oil prices toward post Gulf War highs on Thursday.
In London, February futures for world benchmark crude Brent Blend erased earlier losses to stand nine cents a barrel up on the day at $24.89 at 1755 GMT.
Prices are not far from the $25.06 peak in mid-October, the highest Brent futures price since the Gulf War ended in 1991.
Many traders see little reason for prices to fall much below current levels while the temperatures in both the United States and Europe, the world's biggest heating oil consumers, remain so cold.
"The market's looking in one direction right now and that is up," said Charles Gray, energy analyst at Prudential Bache Futures in London.
Shortly after the open on Thursday, February Brent slumped to a session low of $24.66 on profit-taking after Wednesday's weather-inspired gains. But it later recovered.
The market appears to have shrugged off a bearish U.S. weekly stock report released late Tuesday which showed big gains in U.S. heating oil and gasoline inventories.

Stocks of heating oil and diesel, crude oil and gasoline remain well below where they were this time last year despite the fact that refineries are working flat out to make more product to feed buoyant demand.
"There are still quite a few weeks of winter left. It is too early to sell the market short just yet," a London trader said.
Low industry stocks in consuming countries were the main reason oil prices touched a near six-year high in October last year.
The lean stock situation, a result of oil company tactics to slim down stockpiles to cut costs and free up capital for other investments, has kept a floor under prices for weeks.
Traders are especially wary of selling the market short in case the deep freeze continues for long.

On Thursday, the National Weather Service's six to 10 day outlook called for below normal temperatures in the Northeast. The Weather Services Corp said temperatures could be as much as 15 degrees below normal throughout next week.
